XIIII.}}|{{sc|of the apostles.}}|331}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=14|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Nd}} it came to pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e at Iconium, that they entred together into the {{ls}}ynagogue of the Ievves, and {{ls}}o {{ls}}pake, that a very great multitude of Iewes and of the Greekes did beleeue. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=2}} But the Iewes that were incredulous, {{ls}}tirred vp and incen{{ls}}ed the hartes of the Gentils to anger again{{ls}}t the brethren. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=3}} A long time therfore they abode, dealing confidently in our Lord, vvho gaue te{{ls}}timonie to the vvord of his grace, graunting {{ls}}ignes and vvonders to be done by their handes. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=4}} And the multitude of the citie vvas deuided: and certaine of them in deede vvere vvith the Iewes, but certaine vvith the Apo{{ls}}tles. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=5}} And when the Gentils and the Iewes vvith their princes had made an a{{ls}}{{ls}}ault, to v{{ls}}e them contumeliou{{ls}}ly, and to {{ls}}tone them, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=6}} vnder{{ls}}tanding it, they fled to the cities of Lycaónia, Ly{{ls}}tra and Derbé, and the vvhole countrie about, and there they vvere euangelizing.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=7}} And a certaine man at Ly{{ls}}tra impotent of his feete {{ls}}ate there, lame from his mothers wombe, that neuer had vvalked. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=8}} This {{ls}}ame heard Paul {{ls}}peaking. Vvho looking vpon him, and {{ls}}eeing that he had faith for to be {{ls}}aued, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=9}} he {{ls}}aid vvith a loud voice, Stand vp right on thy feete. And he leaped & vvalked. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=10}} And the multitudes vvhen they had {{ls}}een vvhat Paul had done, lifted vp their voice in the lycaónian tongue, {{ls}}aying, Gods made like to men, are de{{ls}}cended to vs. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=11}} And they called Barnabas, Iupiter: but Paul, Mercurie, becau{{ls}}e he vvas the cheefe {{ls}}peaker. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=12}} The Prie{{ls}}t al{{ls}}o of {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''{{lang|grc|διὸς τοῦ ὄντος}}''}}∷ Iupiter that vvas before the citie, bringing oxen & garlands before the gates, {{sup|‖}} vvould vvith the people {{ls}}acrifice. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=13}} Vvhich thing vvhen the Apo{{ls}}tles Barnabas & Paul heard, renting their coates, they leaped forth into the multitudes, crying {{verse|chapter=14|verse=14}} And {{ls}}aying, Ye men, vvhy doe you the{{ls}}e things? Vve al{{ls}}o are mortal, men like vnto you, preaching to you for to conuert from the{{ls}}e vaine things, to the liuing God that made the heauen, and the earth, and the {{ls}}ea, and al things that are in them: {{verse|chapter=14|verse=15}} vvho in the generations pa{{ls}}t {{ls}}uffred al the Gentils to goe their ovvne vvaies. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=16}} Hovvbeit he left not him {{ls}}elf {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Heathen might by the daily benefites of God haue knowen him at the lea{{ls}}t to haue beene their Creatour and only Lord, though the my{{ls}}terie of our Redemption vvere not opened to them.}}∷ without te{{ls}}timonie, being beneficial from heauen, giuing raines, and fruiteful {{ls}}ea{{ls}}ons, filling our hartes with foode & gladnes. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=17}} And {{ls}}peaking the{{ls}}e things, they {{ls}}car{{ls}}e appea{{ls}}ed<noinclude>{{continues|the}}</noinclude>
